Detailed Description

A list of all mathematical operator type UGen classes and their brief descriptions.

This listas all the arithmetic and mathematical operators which may be applied to UGen instances. This includes the (overloaded) arithmentic operators such as +, -, * and /.

Define Documentation

#define BinaryOpCommonUGenDefinition ( OPNAME   ) 

A BinaryOpUGen usually created using the function OPFUNCTION##() when applied to other UGen instances.

It is not normally required to use this UGen explicitly. 

                UGen result##OPNAME = SinOsc::AR(100, 0, 0.4).##OPFUNCTION##(SinOsc::AR(400, 0, 0.3)); // creates a Binary##OPNAME##UGen

You can also use a global version of this function, the above code would be equivalent as: 

                UGen result##OPNAME = OPFUNCTION##(SinOsc::AR(100, 0, 0.4), SinOsc::AR(400, 0, 0.3)); // creates a Binary##OPNAME##UGen
See also:

OPFUNCTION##(const float leftOperand, UGen const& rightOperand)

 OPFUNCTION##(left, right);

rightOperand The right-hand-side of the oprtation. Global function for the UGen::#OPFUNCTION##() binary operator.
leftOperand The left-hand-side of the operator (a float, double or int)
rightOperand The right-hand-side of the operator.
Returns:
The new UGen which is a result of the OPFUNCTION##() operation.
See also:
UGen::#OPFUNCTION##() Global function for the UGen::#OPFUNCTION##() binary operator. This makes: 
                UGen result##OPNAME = SinOsc::AR(100, 0, 0.4).##OPFUNCTION##(SinOsc::AR(400, 0, 0.3)); // creates a Binary##OPNAME##UGen
..equivalent to: 
                UGen result##OPNAME = OPFUNCTION##(SinOsc::AR(100, 0, 0.4), SinOsc::AR(400, 0, 0.3)); // creates a Binary##OPNAME##UGen
Parameters:
leftOperand The left-hand-side of the operator.
rightOperand The right-hand-side of the operator.
Returns:
The new UGen which is a result of the OPFUNCTION##() operation.
See also:
UGen::#OPFUNCTION##() Return a new Buffer with the binary operator applied to all channels. The resulting Buffer will be the size of the rightOperand and have the same number of channels. The constant leftOperand will be applied to all channels and values using the OPFUNCTION##() function.
Buffer::#OPFUNCTION##(Buffer const& rightOperand) Return a new Buffer with the binary operator applied to all channels. The resulting Buffer will be the size of the largest of the two input Buffers, the smaller Buffer will be effectively padded with zeroes. The resulting Buffer will have a number of channels equal to the highest number of channels in the two input Buffers. When applying the binary operator to two Buffers which have a different number of channels the smaller Buffer's channels will be accessed cyclically (i.e., using wrapped indices).
Buffer::#OPFUNCTION##(Buffer const& rightOperand)

A BinaryOpUGen usually created using the operator OPSYMBOL when applied to other UGen instances.

It is not normally required to use this UGen explicitly. 

                UGen result##OPNAME = SinOsc::AR(100, 0, 0.4) OPSYMBOL SinOsc::AR(400, 0, 0.3); // creates a Binary##OPNAME##UGen
See also:
ugen::operator#OPSYMBOL##(const float leftOperand, UGen const& rightOperand)
UGen::operator#OPSYMBOL##() Construct a Binary#OPNAME#UGen. For symbol-based binary operations these will be from expressions such as: 
 left OPSYMBOL right;

rightOperand The right-hand-side of the operation. Global function for the UGen::operator#OPSYMBOL##() binary operator where the left-hand-side is not a UGen.

Internal for Unary#OPNAME#UGen.

Control rate internal for Unary#OPNAME#UGen. A UnaryOpUGen usually created using the function OPFUNCTION##() when applied to other UGen instances. It is not normally required to use this UGen explicitly. 

                UGen result##OPNAME = SinOsc::AR(100, 0, 0.4).##OPFUNCTION(); // creates a Unary##OPNAME##UGen

You can also use a global version of this function, the above code would be equivalent as: 

                UGen result##OPNAME = OPFUNCTION##(SinOsc::AR(100, 0, 0.4)); // creates a Unary##OPNAME##UGen
See also:
OPFUNCTION##(UGen const& operand)
UGen::#OPFUNCTION##() Global function for OPFUNCTION##(UGen const& operand).
UGen::#OPFUNCTION##() Internal for Unary#OPNAME#Value. Applies the OPFUNCTION##() operator to the input Value. Global function for OPFUNCTION##(Value const& operand).

)

Invert about a particular value.

Implements the expression 

 max-input;

By default this is useful for inverting values around 1.0 e.g., buttons which output 0 or 1 and you want to convert this to 1 and 0 respectively.

See also:
UGen::operator-, UGen::neg(), UnaryOpNegUGen, LinLin

Wrap a UGen with multiply and add inputs.

You may use this directly but it is more common to declare a new UGen by using the macros DirectMulAddUGenDeclaration() or ExpandingMulAddUGenDeclaration() which tests the mul and add inputs to see if the mul and add inputs really need adding.

See also:
BinaryOpMulUGen, BinaryOpAddUGen, UGen::operator*(), UGen::operator+()
